During the Edo period it was called '''Kinomiya Shrine''' (きのみやじんじゃ), and this name is still used today as an alternative name, appearing on items such as the plaque on the torii gate<ref name="kotobank">[https://kotobank.jp/word/白田村-3062457 What is Shirada Village] - Kotobank</ref><ref name="engi-chosa">[http://engishiki.org/izu/bun/iz140133-02.html Shiritaogi Shrine] - Survey of Engishiki Shrines</ref>. {{nihongo|'''Shiritaogi Shrine'''|志理太乎宜神社}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine}} in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932|lt=Engishiki Jinmyōchō}}. It is located in {{ill|Izu Province|ar|مقاطعة إزو|be|Ідзу (правінцыя)|ckb|پارێزگای ئیزو|cs|Provincie Izu|cv|Идзу|de|Provinz Izu|es|Provincia de Izu|fa|ولایت ایزو|fr|Province d'Izu|gl|Provincia de Izu|hak|Yî-theu-koet|id|Provinsi Izu|it|Izu (provincia)|ja|伊豆国|ko|이즈국|lt|Idzu žemė|nl|Izu (provincie)|pl|Prowincja Izu|pt|Província de Izu|ru|Идзу (провинция)|simple|Izu Province|sk|Izu (provincia)|sr|Провинција Изу|th|แคว้นอิซุ|tr|Izu (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Ідзу|zh|伊豆國|zh_min_nan|Izu-kok|zh_yue|伊豆國|qid=Q860928|lt=Izu Province}}.

== Overview ==
The shrine is located immediately west of {{ill|Katase-Shirata Station|ja|片瀬白田駅|ko|가타세시라타역|my|ခတဆဲ - ရှိရတဘူတာ|ur|کاٹاسے-شیراتا اسٹیشن|zh|片瀨白田站|qid=Q6375267}}, along {{ill|Japan National Route 135|af|Japan Nasionale Roete 135|ja|国道135号|zh_min_nan|Ji̍t-pún Kok-tō 135-hō|qid=Q6156779}}.

Together with {{ill|Shiitori Shrine|ja|椎取神社|qid=Q134930749}} on {{ill|Miyake-jima|ar|مياكي جيما|ast|Miyakejima|az|Miyakecima|ceb|Miyake Jima|cs|Mijakedžima|de|Miyake-jima|eo|Mijakeŝimo|es|Miyakejima|fa|میاکجیما|fr|Miyake-jima|it|Miyakejima|ja|三宅島|ko|미야케섬|lt|Mijakedžima|pnb|میاک-جیما|pt|Ilha Miyake|ru|Мияке (остров)|sk|Mijakedžima|sv|Miyakejima|th|เกาะมิยาเกะ|tl|Miyake, Tokyo|tr|Miyakejima|uk|Міяке (острів)|vi|Miyakejima|zh|三宅島|qid=Q1075076}}, it is regarded as a candidate shrine (ronsha) of '''Shirita(ogi) Shrine''' (しりた(お)き[ぎ]じんじゃ), a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} that enshrines Shirita(ogi)-no-Mikoto, one of the princes of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Mishima Daimyōjin}} ({{ill|Kotoshironushi-no-Mikoto|fa|کوتوشیرونوشی|fr|Kotoshironushi|it|Kotoshironushi|ja|事代主|ko|고토시로누시|ru|Котосиронуси|simple|Kotoshironushi|th|โคโตชิโรนูชิ|zh|事代主神|qid=Q8009611|lt=Kotoshironushi-no-Kami}}). Meanwhile, {{ill|Katasuge Shrine|ja|片菅神社 (東伊豆町)|qid=Q134892414|lt=Katasuge Shrine}} in the neighboring Katase district to the north—thought to have been founded around the same time—also serves as a candidate Shikinaisha enshrining another prince of Mishima Daimyōjin (Kotoshironushi-no-Kami) of Miyakejima, competing with {{ill|Katasuge Shrine|ja|片菅神社|qid=Q134930291}} on Miyakejima itself. Because of this branch-shrine–like relationship, it is possible that these shrines were originally established as refugee branch shrines or distant worship sites relocated from Miyakejima to avoid volcanic eruptions<ref name="engi-chosa"/><ref name="engi-chosa2">[http://engishiki.org/izu/bun/iz140116-04.html Katasuge Shrine] - Survey of Engishiki Shrines</ref><ref name="choshi"/>.

Although the date of foundation is unknown, a record of reconstruction in the 2nd year of {{ill|Kōei|ar|فترة كوويه|de|Kōei (Ära)|es|Kōei|fa|کوئی (دوره)|fr|Ère Kōei|ja|康永|ko|고에이 (연호)|ru|Коэй|simple|Kōei (era)|sr|Коеи|sv|Kōei|tr|Kōei|zh|康永|qid=Q980266}} ({{ill|1343|ab|1343|af|1343|als|1343|am|1343 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1343|ar|1343|ary|1343|arz|1343|ast|1343|avk|1343|az|1343|azb|۱۳۴۳ (میلادی)|be|1343|be_x_old|1343|bg|1343|bn|১৩৪৩|bpy|মারি ১৩৪৩|br|1343|bs|1343.|ca|1343|cdo|1343 nièng|ce|1343 шо|ceb|1343|ckb|١٣٤٣|crh|1343|cs|1343|cv|1343|cy|1343|da|1343|de|1343|diq|1343|el|1343|eml|1343|eo|1343|es|1343|et|1343|eu|1343|fa|۱۳۴۳ (میلادی)|fi|1343|fo|1343|fr|1343|fy|1343|ga|1343|gan|1343年|gcr|1343|gd|1343|gl|1343|he|1343|hi|१३४३|hr|1343.|ht|1343 (almanak jilyen)|hu|1343|hy|1343|id|1343|ilo|1343|io|1343|is|1343|it|1343|ja|1343年|jv|1343|ka|1343|kaa|1343|kk|1343 жыл|ko|1343년|krc|1343 джыл|la|1343|lb|1343|lij|1343|lmo|1343|lt|1343 m.|lv|1343. gads|mai|१३४३|map_bms|1343|mdf|1343|mg|1343|mhr|1343|mi|1343|min|1343|mk|1343|mr|इ.स. १३४३|mrj|1343 и|ms|1343|my|၁၃၄၃|mzn|۱۳۴۳|nap|1343|nds|1343|new|सन् १३४३|nl|1343|nn|1343|no|1343|nrm|1343|nso|1343|oc|1343|or|୧୩୪୩|os|1343-æм аз|pl|1343|pnb|1343|pt|1343|qu|1343|ro|1343|ru|1343 год|rue|1343|sa|१३४३|sah|1343|sc|1343|scn|1343|sd|1343ع|se|1343|sh|1343.|shn|1343|simple|1343|sk|1343|sl|1343|smn|1343|sq|1343|sr|1343|su|1343|sv|1343|sw|1343|tg|Соли 1343|th|พ.ศ. 1886|tk|1343|tl|1343|tly|1343|tr|1343|tt|1343 ел|uk|1343|ur|1343ء|uz|1343|vec|1343|vi|1343|vls|1343|war|1343|wuu|1343年|xmf|1343|zh|1343年|zh_min_nan|1343 nî|zh_yue|1343年|qid=Q6072}}) appears in the *Nantō Fudoki*<ref name="choshi">[https://www.town.higashiizu.shizuoka.jp/bg/life/upload/kyo_higashiizutyousi_30mini_6.pdf *History of Higashiizu Town*, Chapter 6, p. 360] - Higashiizu Town</ref>. In addition, ridgepole inscriptions from the 2nd year of {{ill|Jōwa (Muromachi period)|de|Jōwa (Ära)|fa|جووا (دوره)|fr|Ère Jōwa (Nanboku-chō)|ja|貞和|ko|조와 (1345년)|ru|Дзёва (Муромати)|simple|Jōwa (Muromachi period)|sr|Џова (Муромачи период)|sv|Jōwa|tr|Jōwa (Muromachi)|zh|貞和|qid=Q1146143}} ({{ill|1346|ab|1346|af|1346|als|1346|am|1346 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|1346|ar|1346|ary|1346|arz|1346|ast|1346|avk|1346|az|1346|azb|۱۳۴۶ (میلادی)|be|1346|be_x_old|1346|bg|1346|bn|১৩৪৬|bpy|মারি ১৩৪৬|br|1346|bs|1346.|ca|1346|cdo|1346 nièng|ceb|1346|ckb|١٣٤٦|crh|1346|cs|1346|cv|1346|cy|1346|da|1346|de|1346|diq|1346|el|1346|eml|1346|eo|1346|es|1346|et|1346|eu|1346|fa|۱۳۴۶ (میلادی)|fi|1346|fo|1346|fr|1346|fy|1346|ga|1346|gan|1346年|gcr|1346|gd|1346|gl|1346|he|1346|hi|१३४६|hr|1346.|hsb|1346|ht|1346 (almanak jilyen)|hu|1346|hy|1346|id|1346|ilo|1346|io|1346|is|1346|it|1346|ja|1346年|jv|1346|ka|1346|kaa|1346|kk|1346 жыл|ko|1346년|la|1346|lb|1346|lij|1346|lmo|1346|lt|1346 m.|lv|1346. gads|mai|१३४६|map_bms|1346|mdf|1346|mg|1346|mhr|1346|mi|1346|min|1346|mk|1346|mr|इ.स. १३४६|mrj|1346 и|ms|1346|my|၁၃၄၆|mzn|۱۳۴۶|nap|1346|nds|1346|new|सन् १३४६|nl|1346|nn|1346|no|1346|nrm|1346|nso|1346|oc|1346|or|୧୩୪୬|os|1346-æм аз|pl|1346|pnb|1346|pt|1346|qu|1346|ro|1346|ru|1346 год|rue|1346|sa|१३४६|sah|1346|scn|1346|sd|1346ع|se|1346|sh|1346.|shn|1346|sk|1346|sl|1346|smn|1346|sq|1346|sr|1346|su|1346|sv|1346|sw|1346|tg|Соли 1346|th|พ.ศ. 1889|tk|1346|tl|1346|tly|1346|tr|1346|tt|1346 ел|uk|1346|ur|1346ء|uz|1346|vec|1346|vi|1346|vls|1346|war|1346|wuu|1346年|xmf|1346|zea|1346|zh|1346年|zh_min_nan|1346 nî|zh_yue|1346年|qid=Q6080}}) record the name '''Shirada Ki(hama) Shrine''' (しらだき(はま)じんじゃ) (*Zōtei Tōshū Shikō*)<ref name="kotobank"/>.

As indicated by its former shrine name and the enshrined deity {{ill|Isotakeru-no-Mikoto|ja|五十猛神|simple|Isotakeru-no-kami|zh|五十猛神|qid=Q10881556|lt=Isotakeru-no-Mikoto}}, during the Edo period it also strongly exhibited the character of a Kinomiya Shrine associated with {{ill|Kinomiya Faith|ja|キノミヤ信仰|qid=Q11296898}}. Even today, like {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kawazu Kinomiya Shrine}} ({{ill|Sugihokowake no Mikoto Shrine|ja|杉桙別命神社|qid=Q11522170}}) in {{ill|Kawazu, Shizuoka|arz|كاوازو|ceb|Kawazu Chō|es|Kawazu|fa|کاوازو، شیزوئوکا|fr|Kawazu|id|Kawazu, Shizuoka|it|Kawazu|ja|河津町|ko|가와즈정|ms|Kawazu, Shizuoka|my|ခဝဇုမြို့|pl|Kawazu|ru|Кавадзу|tl|Kawazu, Shizuoka|tr|Kawazu|uk|Кавадзу (Сідзуока)|ur|کاوازو، شیزوکا|vi|Kawazu, Shizuoka|zh|河津町|qid=Q1203861}}, it retains the cultural tradition known as “{{ill|bird abstinence and sake abstinence|ja|河津の鳥精進酒精進|qid=Q11553983|lt=bird abstinence and sake abstinence}}”<ref name="engi-chosa"/><ref name="yuisho">On-site shrine history plaque</ref><ref name="ss">[https://www.at-s.com/facilities/article/view/temple/137787.html Kinomiya Shrine (Higashiizu Town)] - Shizuoka Shimbun</ref>.
